From: Tom Baker <legal@acmecorp.com>
To: logan.wright@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA redline + transfer addendum questions

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the quick review on the MSA. Our legal team attached a redline of the DPA (Acme_DPA_redline_v3.docx) and an Order Form transfer addendum. A couple of high-level items they flagged that we want to confirm with Redwood before we escalate to procurement:

- Processor/Controller split: Acme is pushing for clearer language that lists Acme as controller for customer data and Redwood as processor, but they want a limited exception in Section 3.2 for model telemetry (they want explicit permission to ingest hashed model telemetry for billing).
- SCCs: they replaced our SCC annex with EU Commission standard clauses and inserted an extra subparagraph requiring written proof of KMS residency for EU-origin data.
- Transfer addendum: they asked for a fallback routing approach if EU regions are unavailable (they included a short fallback snippet in the Order Form PDF).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the SCCs with an additional KMS attestation (we have KMS in eu-central but need to confirm logistics), and whether we can accept the telemetry carveout if Acme signs a data minimization addendum? Also, please let us know if there are any pricing or SLA implications for the fallback routing language.

Prefer a short call if that helps — Sarah (cc) is our commercial lead and will join.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Baker
Legal Counsel, Acme Logistics

Ben / Laura — forwarding Acme's redline and the addendum. Key asks below (copied from Tom):

1) SCCs + KMS attestation: Acme wants 'written proof' KMS key material is EU-resident. We currently support KMS in eu-central and can provide attestation of key location, but there may be additional ops lead time for a signed certification. Laura — can you confirm whether Legal / Security can issue the attestation letter and an estimated turnaround?

2) Telemetry carveout: Acme requests explicit permission to ingest hashed model telemetry for billing. My read: we can accept a limited telemetry carveout if they sign a short Data Minimization Addendum (we should limit scope to aggregated usage + hashed identifiers, no raw PII). Ben — does this change our billing or model usage terms materially? Any redlines we should push back on?

3) Fallback routing (Order Form): their snippet triggers potential cross-border routing to us-west if eu is unavailable. That could impact transfer controls / surcharge. If we accept, procurement will likely request a surcharge or operational SLA. We should flag pricing impact now.

Suggested next step: Laura to draft the KMS attestation scope + Ben to propose a short telemetry addendum (1 page) and call out any pricing/SLA deltas. I'll consolidate and propose a 30-min sync with Acme tomorrow afternoon.

I'll also attach Acme_DPA_redline_v3.docx to our redline tracker.

— Logan

Subject: RE: Fwd: DPA redline + transfer addendum questions

Logan / Laura — quick thoughts after scanning the redline:

- KMS attestation: Ops can provide a signed attestation that keys are hosted in eu-central. We should limit the attestation to the KMS region and operational controls (who has HSM/admin access). Any wording that suggests we 'guarantee' residency under all contingencies is risky. Proposed language: 'Redwood will maintain KMS keys in the EU region specified in the Order Form and will provide an attestation of key residency and access controls upon request.' Laura — can Legal approve that wording?

- Telemetry carveout: We should accept a conditional carveout limited to hashed, aggregated telemetry used solely for billing and usage reconciliation. We must explicitly exclude training data, raw prompts, and any PII. Add a retention cap (30 days) for hashed telemetry used for reconciliation. Pricing impact: negligible unless they ask for longer retention or real-time streaming to their systems.

- Fallback routing fallback: This is an ops + pricing ask. If we agree to automatic failover to us-west, we should include an availability SLA and a routing surcharge. Suggest we propose: 'automatic fallback permitted up to X hours per month, with surcharge Y per GB and notification to customer.' Laura — procurement will need to surface surcharge ranges.

I'll draft the telemetry addendum (short) and the fallback surcharge bullets. Laura, if you can confirm accept/reject on the KMS attestation language by EOD, I'll stitch together a consolidated response for Acme and propose a 30-min call at 10am PT tomorrow.

Ben Carter
Senior Manager, Product Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: DPA redline + transfer addendum questions — consolidated response and next steps

Tom / Sarah — thanks for the redline and patience while we reviewed with Product Security and Legal. Summary and next steps below.

1) KMS attestation: Redwood can provide a signed attestation confirming that customer-specific KMS keys are hosted in eu-central (AWS eu-central-1) and describing our access controls and HSM boundary. We cannot guarantee residency under catastrophic third-party failure (we'll call that out). Laura will prepare the attestation; target delivery: 3 business days.

2) Telemetry carveout: We can accept the limited telemetry carveout conditional on Acme signing a 1-page Data Minimization Addendum:
   - Scope: hashed, aggregated usage metrics and anonymized counters used only for billing/reconciliation.
   - Exclusions: no raw prompts, no model-training data, no PII.
   - Retention: 30 days (can extend by mutual agreement with surcharge).
Ben has drafted the addendum; attaching our draft and a short comment matrix.

3) Fallback routing / transfer addendum: We can accept the fallback routing language with two conditions:
   - Redwood will provide automatic fallback to us-west for up to 8 hours/month as an operational contingency.
   - Fallback will carry a surcharge (example: $0.04/GB) and will be subject to advance notice and audit during failover events.
This will require a short amendment to the Order Form to capture surcharge and SLA. Procurement will prepare the Order Form wording after you confirm acceptance of the surcharge range.

Next steps / call:
- Laura to deliver KMS attestation (ETA: 3 business days)
- Ben to share telemetry addendum draft (attached)
- Logan to propose Order Form language for surcharge and schedule a 30-min call to finalize

Are you available tomorrow at 10am PT for a short sync? If so we can walk through the attestation and the telemetry addendum and get procurement aligned. If not, happy to propose alternatives.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
